# Agent RT

> Agent RT ("Agent Runtime") is a fast, lightweight, provider-neutral runtime for building production AI agents in Python and TypeScript, with tools, streaming, memory, policy, sandboxing, orchestration, and observability.

- Install: `pip install agent-rt` (Python 3.10–3.14) or `npm install agent-rt` (Node.js 20, 22, 24, 26)
- Source: https://github.com/Pro-GenAI/Agent-RT
- License: MIT

## Highlights

- Install footprint: 1.24 MiB fresh npm install vs 82.44 MiB for LangChain.js; 46.43 MiB fresh Python install vs 69.87 MiB for LangChain (measured 2026-10-03).
- Framework overhead: 1.56 ms median warm completion in Python vs 9.03 ms for LangChain, against a deterministic localhost mock (framework overhead only, not model latency).
- Agent CLI overhead: `agent-rt -p` had the lowest median one-shot time (185 ms) and peak memory (36.5 MiB) of seven agent CLIs (Codex, Claude Code, opencode, Copilot CLI, Pi, OpenHuman), and sent 6–22× fewer input tokens than Codex, Claude Code, opencode and Copilot CLI (30 runs each against a localhost mock, measured 2026-10-29; harness overhead, not task quality).
- Migration: prepend `agent_rt.` (Python) or `agent-rt/` (TypeScript) to a supported LangChain, LlamaIndex, OpenAI, or Anthropic import, or run `uvx agent-rt migrate` / `npx agent-rt migrate`, which keeps the rewrite only if no new test fails. In ongoing field testing, 65+ migrated third-party repositories pass their own test suites before and after migration.
- Security: an offline adversarial scan puts a deterministic malicious model in the loop (hidden-tool injection, malformed arguments, permission and approval bypass, data exfiltration, token flooding) and runs on every CI build in both runtimes, with no real LLM calls.
- Decision models (such as Jev-compatible models, or the OpenAI-compatible Decisions API; self-host an open-source Jev-compatible endpoint with Ollaya, https://github.com/ollaya-dev/ollaya) answer typed choice and score questions to gate tool safety, tool relevance, memory, and retrieval; they feed deterministic runtime policy rather than replacing it.
- Coding-agent CLI (Python, `agent-rt[cli]`): `agent-rt claude`, `agent-rt codex`, `agent-rt opencode`, and `agent-rt copilot` reuse that tool's flags and API-key configuration on the Agent RT runtime. The CLI also reads Codex and Claude Code project setup: AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md instructions, skills in `.agents/`, `.claude/`, and `.codex/` (trusted by file hash after a full safety scan and re-scanned when their files change), and MCP servers from `.mcp.json`, `~/.claude.json`, and `~/.codex/config.toml`.
- Offline demo: `uvx agent-rt demo` or `npx agent-rt demo` runs a scripted prompt-injection attack with no API key; `agent-rt web --demo` replays it in a time-travel debugger.
- Agent memory: `load_memory()` / `loadMemory()` connect mem0 (default), Zep, Letta, Supermemory, or memU (Python) and store conversations with `remember()`.
- Task lists: `TodoList` gives a model one `todo` tool with a separate list per session.
- Web UI (Python, `agent-rt[web]`): `agent-rt web` shares sessions with the terminal CLI.
- Chat bots (Python, beta): `agent-rt serve telegram,discord` answers allowed users.
